findings.evidence: `pointIso` occurs only in its definition, `pointIso_hom`, `pointIso_inv`, and the construction of `pointNatIso` at lines 60–98; the public natural-isomorphism component formulas are already provided at lines 112–129.
findings.fix: Make `pointIso` and its two component lemmas private, retaining `pointNatIso_hom_app` and `pointNatIso_inv_app` as the canonical public component API.
findings.issue: `pointIso` and its hom/inv lemmas duplicate the components of `pointNatIso` and are used only to construct that natural isomorphism, unnecessarily enlarging the public API.

findings.evidence: Lines 167–184 provide only the homomorphism and an equality to `autMulEquivOfIso`/`whiskeringLeft.mapIso`; grep finds no `fgPointNatIsoHom` component lemma, while the all-comodule action has explicit component formulas at lines 112–129.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp]` hom-app and inverse-app lemmas identifying each finite component with the transported `Comodule.pointsAction`, analogous to `pointNatIso_hom_app` and `pointNatIso_inv_app`.
findings.issue: `fgPointNatIsoHom` has no characteristic theorem for its component at a finite comodule; `fgPointNatIsoHom_apply` only exposes the internal whiskering/transport construction, forcing tensor-compatibility consumers to unfold categorical machinery.

summary: The all-comodule action has a usable interface, but the finite action lacks a component theorem and exposes an implementation-only component isomorphism.
